item.title: 2027: Adebutu hails court ruling, says justice has prevailed
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has hailed the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, directing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to restore his name to the list of candidates for the forthcoming governorship election within 24 hours. Adebutu described the judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu on Friday, as a victory for justice, the rule of law and democratic principles. Reacting to the ruling in a statement, the PDP chieftain declared: “Justice has prevailed! Relief is here!” He described the judgment as a significant development in the legal battle over his exclusion from INEC’s published list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun State governorship election. Adebutu said he had consistently maintained that his PDP membership, registration and emergence as the party’s governorship candidate were legitimate and in accordance with due process. “From the moment my name was omitted from INEC’s published list, I maintained that the facts surrounding my PDP membership, registration and the process that produced me as the party’s governorship candidate were clear,” he said. According to him, the party remained confident in the strength of its position and resolved to pursue the matter through the appropriate legal channels. He noted that the judgment had reaffirmed the importance of due process, stressing that political and electoral disputes should be determined on their merits rather than on speculation or premature conclusions. Adebutu expressed appreciation to the national leadership of the PDP, particularly Chief Nyesom Wike, whom he described as the party’s national leader, and its National Chairman, Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed, for their support and confidence throughout the legal proceedings. He also thanked the Ogun State PDP leadership, party members, supporters and residents of the state for their solidarity during the period of uncertainty. “I am equally grateful to the Ogun State PDP leadership, our members, supporters and the good people of Ogun State who remained steadfast. Your patience, encouragement and confidence have been invaluable,” he stated. The governorship candidate also commended the judiciary for its role in upholding justice, emphasising that democratic institutions must remain independent and impartial, irrespective of political interests or affiliations. “Our democratic institutions must remain strong, independent and committed to upholding the law, regardless of political interests or affiliations,” he said. Welcoming the judgment, Adebutu said his focus remained on addressing the developmental challenges confronting Ogun State and engaging residents on practical solutions to improve their welfare. item.title: Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking
item.description: Michael Carrick wished Manchester United “nothing but success” 24 hours after he was sacked, reaffirming his enduring love for the club, who have already appointed Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal, but results have nose-dived in this campaign. The Red Devils are in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 league matches so far. The Old Trafford club named former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino, currently USA head coach, as their new manager on Friday. Despite the downturn this season, Carrick remained popular with supporters in part for his role as a player in multiple triumphs under Alex Ferguson, who retired in 2013. The 45-year-old said his affection remained rock-solid. “I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change,” Carrick wrote in an Instagram post. “I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. “I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.” The former England midfielder paid tribute to the fans, his coaching staff and United’s players. “I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love,” he wrote. “There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. “It’s different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time. “It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.” Carrick described United’s fans as a “special, rare breed”. “We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember,” he said. “The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time. “I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.” The post Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Obi condemns attack on NDC supporters in Lagos, urges peaceful defence of votes
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned the attack on the party’s supporters at a town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday, urging them to remain peaceful while defending their democratic rights. Obi made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Friday, a day after suspected thugs disrupted the party’s gathering in Oregun, Lagos. He said he had been informed that a group of thugs mobilised to attack participants who arrived early for the meeting, noting that he had travelled to Lagos from Abuja to attend a commendation service for Chief Sir Okey Ezibe before proceeding to join supporters at the town hall meeting. “The political violence being enabled by certain political actors against our supporters is an ill wind that blows no one any good. Anarchy consumes everyone,” he said. “We will remain law-abiding, even in the face of extreme provocation.” Obi said the town hall meeting went ahead despite the disruption and participants raised concerns about reviving the economy, the high cost of living, corruption, insecurity, support for vulnerable citizens and the integrity of elections. He said the first responsibility of any government was to secure the country and unite its people around a shared purpose. He also pledged that his administration would pursue policies to reduce living costs, improve welfare and invest in healthcare and education. On the forthcoming elections, the former Anambra governor said protecting the integrity of the process was a shared responsibility, saying the NDC would deploy agents to polling units to observe and document voting, ward collation and the final declaration of results. “I encouraged our people to eschew violence while remaining peaceful, vigilant, and resolute in defending their democratic rights,” he said. Vanguard reported that suspected political thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones invaded the Oregun rally on Thursday, attacking supporters and injuring some participants, although Obi was not at the rally when the incident occurred. item.title: Muniz answers Murphy in three minutes as Fulham hold Newcastle
item.description: Newcastle spent most of Saturday afternoon looking for an opening at Craven Cottage. When Jacob Murphy finally curled the ball past Bernd Leno in the 80th minute, the visitors had a lead that lasted only 179 seconds. Rodrigo Muniz equalised for Fulham in the 83rd, leaving the sides with a 1-1 draw on 7 November 2026. Iwobi and Calvin Bassey both started for Fulham. The match went into the break goalless, a result that has to be kept separate from the full-time draw at betting sites in Cameroon , since the two selections cover different periods. The chances that went begging Fulham were lively early on. Oscar Bobb forced Lukáš Horníček into a save, and Gonzalo García glanced the following corner over. Newcastle soon found a route of their own. Harvey Barnes met an attack from Yoane Wissa and Will Osula, but Leno stopped his close-range finish with a foot. Barnes escaped again and tried to place the ball beyond the goalkeeper. This time Leno got his head to it. Newcastle thought they had scored from the resulting corner when Dan Burn turned in Murphy’s delivery. The goal was ruled out for a foul by Wissa on Timothy Castagne. The official score remained 0-0. It was hardly a first half without attacking chances. Fulham’s Alex Iwobi supplied a cross for Josh King, whose volley brought a sharp save from Horníček. Iwobi picked out King again near the interval, only for the header to go wide. Calvin Bassey also started for the home side, giving the match a second Nigerian international in Fulham’s lineup. The missed opportunities explain why Murphy’s eventual strike looked so decisive. Both goalkeepers had already made stops that could have changed the score considerably earlier. One careless pass, then the reply Newcastle’s goal began with Fulham losing possession in midfield. Murphy collected the loose pass, drove in from the right and bent a left-footed finish beyond Leno. After all the earlier saves, it took one mistake in possession to break the stalemate. Fulham did not leave much time for the away end to celebrate. A high regain put the ball into Shea Charles’s path; he moved it to substitute César Palacios. The attempted cross was blocked, but Muniz reacted to the loose ball and flicked it through a crowd near goal. Muniz had come off the bench earlier in the half. The Premier League said this was his first league goal in 28 matches. His finish came before Newcastle could settle into defending the advantage. item.title: Kane takes Ballon d’Or as England’s wait finally ends
item.description: Twenty-five years after Michael Owen won it, the men’s Ballon d’Or belongs to an Englishman again. Harry Kane picked up the 2026 award at the London Palladium on 26 October, with 73 goals behind his claim. Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé finished second. Kane also left the ceremony with the Gerd Müller Trophy for the leading men’s goalscorer. Comparing a Ballon d’Or forecast through 1xbet South Sudan with a top-scorer selection involves two different results: one comes from a jury, the other from a goal count. Kane collected both honours in London, but they remain separate contests. The numbers behind the London announcement The goals came in two shirts. England Football’s account of the season separates his Bayern appearances from his international ones: Team Appearances Goals Bayern Munich, all competitions 51 61 England, all matches 14 12 Combined 65 73 The league supplied 36 goals in 31 appearances. Kane finished top of the Bundesliga scorers again, for the third year running. He added ten in the DFB-Pokal and one in the Supercup; his European haul was 14 as Bayern went as far as the Champions League semi-finals. Competition names also matter to sports betting in South Sudan , since Kane’s 61 club goals and 36 Bundesliga goals answer different questions. The Champions League figure is part of his club total, rather than an extra contribution to add on top. For England, six goals came in seven World Cup finals appearances. The national side finished third, its best placing since the 1966 victory. The remaining international goals in his season record came in qualifying and friendlies. Five came in five World Cup qualifiers, with another in two international friendly appearances, giving him 12 goals in 14 England outings overall. Bayern’s three domestic trophies give the goals some context, too. They kept the league title and lifted the DFB-Pokal, after winning the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. The Ballon d’Or case included a team collecting silverware while Kane supplied the finishing. Owen’s wait ends, and Bayern’s too Kane becomes the fifth English player to receive the Ballon d’Or. The four names before him cover very different chapters of the award: 1956: Stanley Matthews took the first award. 1966: Bobby Charlton added it to his World Cup year. 1978 and 1979: Kevin Keegan won twice with Hamburg. 2001: Michael Owen brought it to Liverpool. Owen’s victory had remained the last English success for a quarter of a century. Kane’s award adds another name to that short list rather than another win for a previous recipient. Bayern had been waiting even longer. Karl-Heinz Rummenigge was their last winner, back in 1981. The Munich line now runs from Gerd Müller and Franz Beckenbauer through Rummenigge to Kane. item.title: Yiaga Africa: Youth participation in 2027 elections declines by 20%
item.description: Yiaga Africa, an NGO, says the number of young people under 35 expected to participate in the forthcoming general elections has declined by a further 20 per cent, in spite of the enactment of the Not Too Young to Run law. The Executive Director, Yiaga Africa, Dr Samson Itodo, made this known at the Ready To Run Bootcamp for young candidates of political parties under the age of 35 years in Lagos on Friday. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the programme, which is funded by the European Union, has the theme: “Ready to Run Bootcamp: From Aspiration to Representation”. Itodo, represented by its Programme Coordinator, Mr Ibrahim Faruk, said that following the passage of the law in 2019 by President Muhammadu Buhari, young people under 35 constituted 38 per cent of candidates in the 2019 general elections The executive director said that the percentage further dropped to about 28 per cent in 2023. Itodo attributed the decline to the high costs for nomination forms, campaigning, along with party structures and primary control among others. The executive director added that this leaned toward established interests, which had pushed young people to the margins and made securing political tickets difficult. He said: “The first thing Yiaga is doing is what we are doing here today, you know, there is the narrative that says young people are not ready to run. “Yiaga Africa is also changing that narrative to say young people are ready to run, and we are doing that through the Ready to Run boot camps to ensure that young people are ready to run. “​We have also done a lot of electoral reform advocacy; a lot of the changes to the Electoral Act have been as a result of advocacy. ​”While there have been attempts to reduce the high cost of nominations, also ensure that parties are more democratic and inclusive in a way that supports young people. “​Some of these advocacy efforts have been fruitful, some of them have taught us lessons. “We will continue to advocate for an electoral process that accommodates more young people, is more inclusive, less expensive and as democratic as possible,” he said. ​Itodo urged INEC and stakeholders to emphasise on ensuring a credible, secure, and logistically sound electoral process that the outcomes would reflect the will of the people. He also urged young Nigerians to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), participate fully and peacefully as voters, candidates, or agents, and refuse to sit out the democratic process. In his remarks, the Founder, African Governance Institute for Development, Mr Seyi Adisa admitted that running for office was more difficult for young people, as elections required not only financial resources but also “social capital”. According to him, while older individuals generally have more experience and social capital, young people can win elections. “It is more difficult, but achievable with the right strategies, networks, coalitions, and alliances,”he said. item.title: Ebola: Nigeria records zero secondary infections as 62 contacts exit monitoring
item.description: … Index patient recovers, discharged in Switzerland By Chioma Obinna Nigeria has recorded zero secondary transmission of the deadly Bundibugyo Virus Disease, a form of Ebola, following the successful completion of the 21-day monitoring period for all 62 contacts linked to the imported case confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on October 20, 2026. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) yesterday announced that the last contact had been discharged from monitoring, with none of the 62 individuals developing the disease. In another development, the index patient, who was medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment, has recovered, subsequently tested negative for the virus and been discharged from hospital. However, the NCDC warned that the successful completion of contact monitoring does not amount to a formal declaration that the outbreak is over, insisting that Nigeria must sustain heightened surveillance amid continued Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, who announced the development, described the outcome as encouraging, crediting early detection, prompt investigation and cooperation between health authorities and affected communities. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case,” Idris said. He disclosed that 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease and returned negative results. Similarly, seven alerts reported in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the last three weeks were investigated, with laboratory tests confirming that none was positive for the virus. The NCDC boss explained that the imported case was detected following an alert raised by healthcare workers through the agency’s event-based surveillance system, enabling the government to activate an emergency response and commence investigations. Under the leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, the National Emergency Operations Centre was activated, while an Incident Management System was established to coordinate the response. According to Idris, the response focused on providing clinical care, identifying and monitoring exposed persons, preventing further transmission, protecting healthcare workers and strengthening disease surveillance. He said contact tracing covered healthcare facilities, households and other relevant settings, while infection prevention and control measures were reinforced in health facilities within the FCT and across the country. item.title: 2027: Obanikoro confident of Tinubu, Hamzat’s victory
item.description: Sen. Musiliu Obanikoro, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu and the party’s governorship candidate in Lagos State, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, will emerge victorious in the 2027 general elections. Obanikoro, Director-General, PBAT-KOH Campaign Council, Lagos State, gave the expressed this while speaking during the Lagos SWAGA 2.0 Summit and launch in Lagos, on Friday. He said the party was well positioned to win Lagos, adding that the achievements of the Tinubu administration at the federal level and those of the Lagos State Government had endeared the APC to the electorate. “We are confident of victory. President Tinubu has shown leadership, and Hamzat has the experience and capacity to sustain the progress of Lagos. “Lagos residents know what good governance looks like, and they will not gamble with their future “I commend the grassroots mobilisation and initiative of SWAGA 2.0 for mobilising supporters to this event venue. “With this great turnout, massive victory is assured for Tinubu and APC gubernatorial candidate, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, ” he said. Obanikoro tasked party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation and ensure the party delivered 3.5 million votes for Tinubu and Hamzat in the state He said the target was achievable if members remained united, disciplined and committed to the party’s campaign structure. “Our target is 3.5 million votes. It is not just a number, it is a statement that Lagos stands firmly behind Tinubu and Hamzat,” he said. He urged party leaders at ward and local government levels to take the campaign to every polling unit and engage voters on the party’s achievements. Obanikoro said the opposition lacked the structure and credibility to challenge the APC in Lagos, describing the party as the only party with a clear vision for the state and the country. He called on supporters to shun violence and conduct issue-based campaigns, stressing that the APC would win through performance, not intimidation. “We must campaign with our records. We must not engage in violence. Our victory will come from the people because they have seen what we have done,” he said. He assured supporters that the party leadership would provide the necessary support to ensure a hitch-free campaign and victory at the polls. item.title: 95,000 PVCs uncollected in Plateau – INEC
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), says more 95,000 Permanent Voters Cards (PVCs) have not been collected in Plateau. Prof. Samuel Egwu, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, disclosed this during a press conference on Friday in Jos. The REC explained that the uncollected PVCs were largely for those who registered before the 2023 general elections. Egwu, who said that the commission was worried over the large number of unclaimed PVCs in the state, urged voters to take advantage of the ongoing distribution exercise to collect their PVCs. “More than 95,000 PVCs from 2023 were still with our Electoral Officers across the state. “We call on who those who registered before the last general elections to come and collect their PVCs to enable them participate in the 2027 general elections,”he advised. The REC said that PVCs from the first phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise conducted between August and December 2025, were made available for collection at INEC offices across the 17 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of the state. He said particularly that the PVCs of Shendam, Langtang North, Jos South and Kanam, were now available for collection. “More than 19,000 PVCs for those who applied for transfers and corrections are also available for collection. “All PVCs for the second phase of CVR conducted between January and April, are available and have been taken to the 17 LGAs for collection. “PVCs for the third phase of CVR are not ready, but will be made available before the end of November for collection,”he said. Egwu also disclosed that all non-sensitive materials for the 2027 general elections were available at the INEC office in Jos and would soon be distributed to the 17 LGAs. He further said that training of electoral officers who were not trained in 2023 had commenced. The REC reiterated INEC’s readiness to conduct a credible election in 2027. item.title: 2027: How to secure victory for Tinubu, APC — Banire
item.description: A former legal adviser to the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Muiz Banire, has urged members of the South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA) 2.0,a support group,to campaign aggressively with the achievements of President Bola Tinubu to secure victory for him. Banire,a former commissioner of transportation in Lagos,made the call during the SWAGA 2.0 Summit and official launch in Ikeja, on Friday. He said political rallies alone were not sufficient to secure electoral victory. The chieftain said there was need for sustained grassroots mobilisation and direct engagement with voters. According to him, campaigns should not be characterised by abuses, confrontation or unnecessary political arguments but should focus on educating the electorate about government policies, programmes and achievements. “Rallies are not what win elections. What wins elections is going from door to door, engaging the people and explaining to them what the government has achieved. “Campaigns should not be about abusing opponents or engaging in fights. They should be about educating the electorate and convincing voters with facts about the performance of the present administration,” he said. Banire urged SWAGA leadership to establish functional campaign teams across all wards, local government areas and local council development areas in the South-West to strengthen grassroots mobilisation. He advised the organisation to compile and coordinate information on registered All Progressives Congress (APC) voters in the various communities to facilitate effective voter engagement and mobilisation. “SWAGA must ensure that it has representatives in every ward and local government area. You must know your people, understand the voting strength in each locality and develop a strategy for reaching them. “Wherever members or campaign agents encounter challenges in the course of their assignments, they should report such issues to their respective leaders for prompt attention and necessary solutions,” he said. The former commissioner emphasised the importance of appointing competent and literate campaign agents who could communicate effectively with residents and provide accurate information about government policies and achievements. He added that campaign and party agents must be able to read, write and understand the issues they are expected to communicate to the electorate. Banire expressed confidence that the South-West would deliver at least 70 per cent of its votes to President Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election if party members remained committed to effective grassroots mobilisation. item.title: NDC attack: NYCN warns Lagos youths against political thuggery
item.description: The National Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN), Lagos State Chapter, has warned youths against allowing themselves to be recruited or manipulated into political thuggery. The youth organisation gave the warning following the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Lagos. The council’s Chairman,Ibrahim Adigun, spoke with the interview with the News Agency of Nigeria on Friday in Lagos. Adigun said no amount of financial inducement or promise of political patronage was worth the life, freedom or future of any young person. He urged Lagos youths to recognise their importance as stakeholders in the democratic process and channel their energies towards peaceful political participation, civic responsibility and nation-building. “No amount of financial inducement or promise of political patronage is worth a life, a criminal record or a future destroyed. “As young people, we must recognise that we are stakeholders in the democratic process and we should channel our energy towards peaceful participation, civic responsibility and nation-building. “For emphasis, the NYCN Lagos State Chapter maintains its unequivocal opposition to political thuggery, electoral violence and every form of intimidation,” he said. Adigun said the council would continue to advocate peaceful political participation, responsible youth engagement and an electoral environment where every citizen could freely express their political choices without fear. He described the attack on NDC supporters as a serious threat to democratic participation, peaceful political engagement and the safety of citizens. According to him, political differences, no matter how deeply held, must never be settled through violence, intimidation or destruction of property. He expressed sympathy with those injured or otherwise affected by the incident, particularly young people, and wished them a speedy and full recovery. The NYCN chairman urged the relevant authorities to identify and bring those responsible for the attack to justice. He also appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to embrace civility and tolerance as political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gathered momentum. “Campaigns should be driven by ideas, policies, track records and credible alternatives capable of addressing the concerns of Nigerians, particularly young people,” he said. Adigun called on security agencies, particularly the Lagos State Police Command, to strengthen security arrangements around political gatherings and other public events. He urged the agencies to remain professional, impartial and proactive in identifying potential threats, preventing attacks and protecting lives and property, irrespective of political affiliations. The chairman also reiterated the council’s commitment to opposing political thuggery, electoral violence and all forms of intimidation. item.title: Ondo APC assures of unity, readiness for 2027 elections
item.description: The Ondo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) says it is united and committed to securing victory for President Bola Tinubu and other candidates in the 2027 general elections. The APC State Chairman, Mr Babatunde Kolawole, said this on Friday in Akure at a news conference organised by the party. Kolawole also dismissed concerns over alleged internal divisions, saying reconciliation efforts were yielding positive results with no exclusion of any member. He dismissed claims of rivalry among party leaders, insisting that members belonged to the same political family and should not regard one another as opponents. According to him, there is no basis for rivalry, particularly as there won’t be governorship election in Ondo in 2027 while President Tinubu has emerged as the party’s sole presidential candidate. “Therefore, there is no rivalry. There is no cause for alarm. I can assure you we are on top of it and everything will be okay,” he said. The chairman appreciated Tinubu and the APC National Chairman for their support, while commending the Senate Leader, Sen. Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, and other party members for their contributions to the success of the presidential campaign. Also, Mr Victor Olabimtan, Director-General, State APC Presidential Campaign Council, said the reconciliation committee constituted after the party congress had reached out to party organs, interest groups and individuals across the country. Olabimtan said the committee had visited Abuja to engage some party leaders, while others were contacted in Lagos and different parts of the country. “We had Mr Wale Akinterinwa and Princess Oladunni Odu at the recent presidential campaign rally in the state as evidence of progress in the reconciliation process. “Nobody is left out. All we need to do is to ensure that we put more effort into strengthening the existing unity that we are all enjoying in the party today. “So, there is no cause for alarm. As we make progress, you will also see that our efforts, the efforts of the governor, the party and its leaders are indeed yielding fruits to ensure that everybody is brought on board,” he said. Similarly, state Commissioner for Women Affairs, Dr Seun Osamaye, pledged the support of women across the state for Tinubu’s re-election, saying collective mobilisation was essential to achieving the party’s one million votes target. Meanwhile, an APC chieftain, Chief Olusola Oke, dismissed concerns about political thuggery ahead of the 2027 elections, saying Ondo remained peaceful and no opposition member or political party had been attacked by thugs. item.title: Benue APC Campaign Council rejects Akume-led coalition for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: ..alleges plot against Alia’s re-election By Peter Duru, Makurdi Benue State All Progressives Congress, APC, Tinubu/Alia Campaign Council, has opposed the emergence of the Senator George Akume-led Strategic Alliance for Tinubu/Shettima Re-election 2027, alleging that the group is being used as a platform to undermine Governor Hyacinth Alia’s political fortunes ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The party expressed concern over the involvement of some prominent APC chieftains, including Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, and Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation, Professor Joseph Utsev, in the alliance, which it claimed also accommodates opposition figures and governorship candidates. The Director-General of the Tinubu/Alia 2027 Campaign Council in Benue State, Citizen Richard Asema, stated the party’s position during a press briefing insisting that the alliance was unnecessary and could create divisions within the APC while threatening its electoral prospects in the state. Asema said, “The Benue State Chapter of All Progressives Congress (APC) views with serious concern the purported formation of the ‘Strategic Alliance For Tinubu/Shettima Re-election 2027’ by some political individuals and groups and the subsequent announcement of a Campaign Council for the re-election of our dear President, Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “The Party observes that this ‘Strategic Alliance’ is populated by some members of the APC, some of whom are holding senior positions in the Federal Government of Nigeria, including Senator George Akume, Secretary to Government of the Federation (SGF) and Prof Joseph Utsev, Hon. Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation. “A critical look at the membership of this so-called Campaign Council reveals that governorship candidates of other political parties, especially the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Labour Party (LP), as well as officers of some other minority parties, are members of the Group and its ‘Campaign Council’. “The APC in Benue State under the leadership of Rev Fr Hyacinth Alia and the Chairmanship of Benjamin Omale, wishes to strongly reject this purported Strategic Alliance and its Campaign Council. “This Council, to say the least, is contemptuous and injurious to the fortunes of APC and its electioneering machinery in the state as being coordinated by His Excellency, Rev Fr Dr Hyacinth Alia. “From all credible intelligence available to the party, this Strategic Alliance has a hidden agenda, which is to sabotage the election of Rev Fr Hyacinth Alia in the 2027 elections, while masquerading as supporters of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “The APC in Benue State recently constituted a comprehensive Campaign Council with over 900 loyal and credible party leaders as members. item.title: With my record in Oyo, I’ll win 2027 — Makinde
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde says his record in the state gives him confidence ahead of the 2027 election, pointing to increases in the state’s minimum wage, regular salary payments, investment in agriculture and infrastructure, and support for moving local produce to international markets as achievements he believes will help win voters’ support and edge him above other candidates. In an interview with Arise Television on Friday, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate contrasted his administration’s approach with the Federal Government’s economic policies, arguing that national reforms should be judged by their impact on people’s daily lives. He also said economic growth and higher reserves meant little if Nigerians remained hungry and families could not afford basic needs. “Taking little reforms here and there will not work. If you are saying that things are happening at the macro level but it will filter down to micro, I see these as just excuses and shifting blames. Explaining, so we have very high reserves. What’s the impact on the ordinary people on the street? Are Nigerians hungry? Are more families able to, you know, afford certain things?” Makinde said. He cited increases in the minimum wage in Oyo State during his time as governor, saying it had risen from N18,000 to N30,000 and later to between N70,000 and N80,000. “How about the salary? Since I came in, I met a minimum wage at 18,000 naira, and we moved it to 30,000, all within seven plus years. When this administration started in 2023, I mean things basically went haywire, and we moved again minimum wage to 70-75, 80,000 naira,” he said. Makinde added that the state had not delayed salary payments during his tenure, including throughout the Buhari administration. “We have never held salaries for one month out of the seven plus years that I’ve spent here in Oyo State, all through the President Buhari period in office, we paid salaries. Oyo State never owed salaries under my watch,” he said. The governor said his administration had sought to expand Oyo’s economy by using the state’s agricultural advantage and investing in infrastructure. He said the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency was established to support the sector. “Here in Oyo State, we said, ‘Look, we will expand our economy using agriculture because obviously we have a comparative advantage in agriculture.’ When we came in, we set up Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency, and also we said we will use development of our infrastructure to also drive our economy,” he said. Makinde linked infrastructure investment to the cost of living, saying transportation costs affect the movement of goods and services and contribute to prices. “When you are talking about structural cost of living. Transportation is a major part of it. To move goods and services from one area to the other, they all contribute to the structural cost of living, and it’s quite major,” he said. He also criticis

item.title: England’s most capped players in history as Kane sets record [Top 5]
item.description: England captain Harry Kane has become the country’s most-capped men’s footballer of all time after making his 126th international appearance in the Three Lions’ UEFA Nations League clash against Croatia on Thursday. The Bayern Munich striker surpassed former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, who previously held the record with 125 appearances for England between 1970 and 1990. Kane achieved the milestone when he started against Croatia at Wembley Stadium, becoming the first England men’s player to reach 126 senior international caps. The 33-year-old was honoured before kick-off, with Shilton presenting him with a commemorative award, while Prince William handed him a special shirt bearing the number 126. Kane also marked the occasion on the pitch, scoring a penalty in England’s 2-1 victory over Croatia to increase his international goals tally to 92. The striker, who made his England debut against Lithuania in March 2015, already holds the national team’s all-time goalscoring record, having moved past Wayne Rooney’s previous mark of 53 goals in March 2023. The Guardian+2 Here are England’s five most-capped men’s players in history. 1. Harry Kane – 126 appearances Kane sits at the top of England’s all-time appearance chart after overtaking Shilton with his 126th cap against Croatia. Since making his international debut in 2015, the striker has established himself as one of the country’s most influential players, captaining the national team and becoming its leading goalscorer. He won the Golden Boot at the 2018 FIFA World Cup, helping England reach the semi-finals, and subsequently led the Three Lions to the final of Euro 2020 and Euro 2024. His international record includes 92 goals in 126 appearances, making him both England’s most-capped men’s player and its leading goalscorer. 2. Peter Shilton – 125 appearances Former goalkeeper Peter Shilton held England’s appearance record for 36 years before Kane surpassed him. Shilton represented England between 1970 and 1990, accumulating 125 caps during an international career spanning two decades. He featured at three FIFA World Cups, in 1982, 1986 and 1990, as well as the 1984 and 1988 European Championships. The former Nottingham Forest goalkeeper was part of England’s squad that reached the semi-finals of the 1990 World Cup in Italy, where they lost to West Germany on penalties. Shilton also recorded 66 clean sheets for England during his international career. 3. Wayne Rooney – 120 appearances Wayne Rooney occupies third place with 120 appearances for England, having represented the national team between 2003 and 2018. The former Manchester United and Everton forward made his international debut as an 17-year-old against Australia in February 2003. He went on to become one of England’s most important players, scoring 53 goals and holding the national team’s goalscoring record until Kane surpassed him in 2023. Rooney featured in three World Cups and three European Championships during his international career

item.title: Atiku wanted me as running mate in 2023 – Makinde
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has revealed that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar approached him to be his running mate in the 2023 presidential election, but he declined the offer because he considered himself inexperienced in public service at the time. Makinde disclosed this during an interview on ARISE News, where he spoke about his political journey, his relationship with members of the G5 governors, the crisis within the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and his political ambitions. The governor said he was approached to run alongside Atiku but turned down the offer, explaining that he had only spent three years in office as governor of Oyo State. He said, “Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and his people approached me to run with him. I basically told them that I had only spent three years as governor of Oyo State and three years in public service. I felt it was not enough to make such a decision, so I told them to look for someone else.” Speaking on the G5 governors’ decision to oppose Atiku’s presidential ambition in 2023, Makinde said he was the only member of the group who had since left the PDP. He also defended the decision by his faction to expel former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike from the party, saying it was necessary after Wike declared his intention to hold the PDP for President Bola Tinubu. Makinde said the decision was aimed at allowing the party to participate in the election, even if it meant going to the polls with a weakened structure. He, however, expressed concern over the state of Nigeria’s democracy, questioning why political parties were still dealing with the nullification of candidates less than 80 days before a national election. “Why? What kind of democracy is that?” he asked. Reacting to allegations by the Oyo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he had abandoned governance to pursue his political campaign, Makinde defended his activities outside the state. He argued that if the President could travel around the country for political activities, governors should also be allowed to take their messages to Nigerians. Makinde maintained that governance in Oyo State had continued despite his political engagements, citing his presentation of the 2027 budget estimates to the State House of Assembly and his state-of-the-state address. “Oyo State is moving on. We have robust institutions, and I am not outside the country,” he said. On his preferred successor, Bimbo Adekanbi, Makinde dismissed suggestions that his support for the former commissioner made him a political godfather. He explained that Adekanbi emerged through a consensus process which he supported, but insisted that his successor should be allowed to establish his own political identity. “I have told him severally, ‘Bimbo, don’t inherit my enemies or opponents. Chart your own path.’ I am interested in good governance,” he said. The governor also ruled out becoming a political godfather, insisting that his backg

item.title: 2027: My presidential bid may have upset Tinubu — Makinde
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate Seyi Makinde says he believes his presidential ambition may have caused “bad blood” between him and President Bola Tinubu, whom he supported in the 2023 election, adding that he could only speculate that people may have told Tinubu he was also considering a run. Makinde made the remarks during an interview with Arise Television on Friday, while discussing how his relationship with Tinubu changed after he helped the President win votes in Oyo State in 2023. He also recalled meeting Tinubu when the FCT Minister Nyesom Wike told him he would hold the PDP for him ahead of the 2027 elections. “Well, I can only guess. Yes, please. You know, people talk a lot. Maybe some people went and told him, ‘Look, Seyi may likely run against you.’ I don’t know. That may cause bad blood between us,” Makinde said. “We were with the president and the minister of FCT. You know, knelt just by his side and told him that, look, I will hold PDP for you.” Makinde also said he supported Wike during the 2023 PDP presidential primary which meant he could not have been driven by an ambition to run. He added that he had also declined an approach from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s associates to join him on a ticket in 2023, saying he had not been governor or a public servant long enough to take on the role. He added: “So, it was my ambition, but I supported him in 2023 during the presidential primary of PDP. So, I didn’t have ambition then. I suddenly just developed an ambition. And let me say this: former VP Atiku Abubakar had his people approach me to run with him, and I basically told them, ‘Look, I was only three years as a governor in Oyo State, and three years as a public servant. So it wasn’t enough to take such a decision.’ So I said to them, ‘No, go look for someone else that can run. If it’s an ambition driving me, that is probably the surest part.” Makinde also said Tinubu did not contact him during the 56 days pupils and teachers abducted in Oriire Local Government Area remained in captivity. He said he had tried to see the President because he expected him to show concern over the kidnapping. “I tried to see the President when our students and our children and their teachers were kidnapped, because I thought if any part of Nigeria is going through such a challenge, the president should be interested. Actually, I expected the president to call me,” he said. Asked whether Tinubu eventually contacted him, Makinde replied: “He did not. No. Till tomorrow.” The governor said he also tried to reach the President through the State Chief of Protocol but received no response. He said he had never spoken directly with Tinubu about anything and was focused on governing Oyo State. “I’m saying it again that till tomorrow I’ve not spoken directly with the President about anything. I’m just minding my own business, running Oyo State. And I’m not complaining,” he said. The abdu

item.title: Ogun 2027: PDP celebrates Adebutu ruling, vows to reclaim state
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Following a fresh boost to Hon. Ladi Adebutu’s candidacy, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has vowed to reclaim Ogun State in the 2027 governorship election, urging residents to rally behind its candidate and other party flag-bearers. The party made the declaration while reacting to a Federal High Court judgment ordering the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to reinstate Adebutu as its governorship candidate, saying the ruling had strengthened its determination to return to power in the state. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, the PDP welcomed the judgment as a victory for democracy, justice and the rule of law. The party said the development had energised its members, supporters and stakeholders as it intensified preparations for the 2027 general elections. It urged the people of Ogun State to rally behind Adebutu and other PDP candidates, promising a government focused on economic opportunities, infrastructure, education and healthcare. “Our desire and commitment is to build an Ogun state where economic opportunities are expanded, infrastructure is strengthened, education and healthcare receive the attention they deserve, and government genuinely serves the interests of the people,” Jungudo said. The PDP expressed confidence that a fresh mandate from Ogun residents would enable it to pursue the state’s developmental aspirations and improve the living conditions of its citizens. “The journey to reclaim Ogun State and restore purposeful governance is firmly on course,” the party declared. item.title: Attack on NDC supporters in Lagos cowardly — Ladipo Johnson
item.description: Mr Ladipo Johnson, Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Lagos Central Senatorial candidate, has described the attack on supporters of the party in Lagos as cowardly, premeditated and unprovoked. Johnson made the condemnation in Lagos on Friday, while reacting to the disruption of the party’s town hall meeting at the Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that NDC supporters had gathered at the venue ahead of a town hall meeting with the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi. Johnson said the incident should not be regarded as a feud between political groups, stressing that those attacked were law-abiding citizens exercising their democratic rights. “First, let me clarify that what transpired yesterday along Kudirat Abiola Way in Oregun, Ikeja, was not a feud. A feud implies a mutual dispute between two parties. “What we witnessed yesterday was a premeditated, unprovoked and cowardly attack on peaceful, law-abiding citizens and supporters of the NDC,” he said. He said the incident was deeply troubling and reflected growing concerns about political intimidation and violence ahead of the 2027 general elections. Johnson called on political leaders to be mindful of their public statements, arguing that inflammatory rhetoric could embolden supporters to resort to violence. “We must call a spade a spade. The audacity displayed by these hoodlums does not exist in a vacuum. When the leadership of a nation uses rhetoric that frames power as something to ‘grab, snatch and run with’, it sends a dangerous signal,” he said. He called on President Bola Tinubu to personally address Nigerians and condemn the incident, urging him to direct state governors and security agencies to take decisive measures against political violence. “It is simply not enough for the All Progressives Congress (APC) to issue routine statements distancing itself from the violence. “If the administration is truly committed to democracy and the rule of law, President Tinubu must personally address the nation, unequivocally condemn yesterday’s attack and read the riot act to state governors, the Inspector-General of Police and the heads of all security agencies,” he said. Johnson warned that failure to take decisive action could undermine public confidence in the government’s commitment to protecting democratic rights. He maintained that the incident would not discourage the NDC from exercising its constitutional rights or engaging voters across Lagos State. “If the intention behind yesterday’s attack was to instil fear in our supporters or disrupt our momentum in Lagos, it has failed woefully. “The NDC and the broader opposition will not be cowed. We will stand our ground whenever and wherever we are attacked or intimidated,” he said. item.title: [UPDATED] Manchester United Announce Pochettino As New Manager After Carrick Sacking
item.description: Manchester United on Friday announced that Mauricio Pochettino would be their new manager following the dismissal of Michael Carrick. The club issued a statement saying the USA coach, who has previously managed Tottenham and Chelsea in the Premier League, would take charge from November 18. The 54-year-old is understood to have signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford, taking him through to the end of the 2028/29 season. “The club has reached an agreement with the US soccer federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team,” United said. “The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.” “Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues.” Pochettino, who led the United States to the last-16 of the World Cup on home soil earlier this year, said in a statement released by US Soccer that the job with the national team had been “one of the greatest honours of my career”. “We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country,” he added. US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson said Pochettino had left a lasting mark on football in the United States through his “leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture”. The federation is reportedly set to receive $10 million in compensation for him, plus a further $2 million for the departure of his coaching staff. Pochettino has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea in England, and also coached Paris Saint-Germain. He never finished lower than fifth in the Premier League during his five seasons at Tottenham. But despite his relative success at Spurs, Pochettino failed to win silverware and was dismissed in November 2019 — just months after the north London club lost to Liverpool in the Champions League final. He claimed the first trophies of his managerial career with PSG, collecting the 2021 French Cup and 2022 Ligue 1 title, but did not see out his contract. Pochettino returned to the dugout at Chelsea in 2023 but lasted a single season, reaching the FA Cup semi-finals and losing in the League Cup final. item.title: How Flamingos Ended Africa’s Long Wait For Women’s World Cup Glory
item.description: For decades, African football has produced teams capable of challenging the world’s best, but winning a FIFA World Cup title has remained an elusive ambition for the continent’s women’s national teams. That long wait finally ended on Saturday, November 7, 2026, when Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, conquered the world in Morocco. A hard-fought 2-1 victory over Japan in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup secured Nigeria’s maiden title in the competition and made the Flamingos the first African women’s national team to win a FIFA World Cup trophy at any level. The Flamingos celebrating their victory at the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup Goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, scored in the 39th and 47th minutes respectively, gave Nigeria a two-goal advantage before Japan’s Fuki Ito reduced the deficit in the 80th minute. The Nigerian girls, however, showed remarkable composure under pressure to protect their lead and write their names into football history. It was a victory that meant considerably more than another trophy for Nigeria. It represented a breakthrough for African women’s football and demonstrated that the continent’s young talents could go all the way against the established powers of the game. ﻿ A Journey Defined By Resilience The road to the trophy was far from straightforward. The Flamingos began their campaign with a disappointing 2-1 defeat to Poland, raising questions about their readiness to compete for the title. However, rather than allow the setback to derail their ambitions, the Nigerian girls responded with character and determination, winning their remaining six matches to complete a remarkable turnaround. They returned to winning ways with a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the biggest statements of the tournament by defeating defending champions North Korea 3-1. The result ended the Asian side’s 18-match unbeaten run in regulation time at the competition and announced Nigeria as a serious contender. The Flamingos maintained their momentum in the knockout stages, defeating Mexico 2-1 in the Round of 16. Oluebube Umejiaku and Mary Dunstan found the net to send Nigeria into the quarter-finals. Azeezat Oduntan then emerged as the match-winner against Venezuela, converting a late penalty in the 89th minute to secure a 1-0 victory and book Nigeria’s place in the last four. But the Flamingos delivered an emphatic performance, defeating the South Americans 3-1 to reach their first-ever final at the competition. Queen Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute before Awawu Bashiru struck twice, in the 71st and 80th minutes, to put Nigeria firmly in control. Brazil managed a late consolation, but it was not enough to prevent the Nigerian side from securing a historic place in the final. Kirubakaran, who represented the Vice-Chancellor, described the ceremony as a landmark achievement for the Faculty and urged the newly inducted engineers to uphold the values of integrity, responsibility and continuous learning throughout their careers. item.title: Is Galadima the Round Peg in the Round Hole for Adamawa?
item.description: In Nigerian politics, the phrase “a round peg in a round hole” is often used to suggest that a candidate’s temperament, experience and timing align perfectly with the demands of the moment. In Adamawa State, that description is increasingly being attached to Ahmed Tijjani Galadima, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for 2027. But is he truly the right fit for Adamawa’s complex political and developmental realities, or simply the beneficiary of strategic party consensus? Adamawa is no ordinary political battleground. Situated in Nigeria’s North-East, the state has long balanced agricultural potential with security challenges, urban expansion with rural neglect, and a politically vibrant electorate with shifting party loyalties. Governorship contests here are rarely predictable. Personal networks, regional considerations, grassroots mobilisation and elite consensus all play decisive roles—and often collide. Galadima’s emergence as the APC’s standard-bearer was no accident. A seasoned technocrat, he previously served as Executive Secretary of the Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), a position that placed him at the intersection of public administration, human capital development and federal policymaking. Within policy circles, that experience is often cited as evidence of administrative competence—a quality many voters say has become increasingly important after years of governance characterised more by political brinkmanship than institutional reform. Within the APC, his candidacy also represents consolidation. Several key aspirants stepped aside before and during the primary process, sparing the party the bruising internal contest that has weakened it in previous election cycles. For a party seeking to reclaim power in Adamawa from the administration of Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, unity is more than desirable; it is essential. Galadima’s ability to attract support across competing blocs suggests he enjoys both political goodwill and strategic alliances. Yet politics in Adamawa extends beyond party arithmetic. The electorate remains deeply concerned about security, particularly in communities affected by the spillover of insurgency in the North-East. Farmers want safer farmlands, traders need secure transport corridors, and young people seek economic opportunities that do not require leaving the state. Any candidate seeking to be regarded as the “right fit” must present credible solutions to these interconnected challenges. Supporters argue that Galadima’s administrative experience positions him to drive economic renewal. Adamawa’s economy remains largely agrarian, with significant untapped potential in agro-processing, livestock production and cross-border trade with neighbouring Cameroon. With improved infrastructure, targeted investment incentives and better access to rural finance, the state could move beyond subsistence agriculture towards value-added production. item.title: Violent campaigns
item.description: Barely two months to the 2027 general elections, there are rising cases of political violence across Nigeria, despite efforts by various bodies to discourage mayhem before, during and after the polls. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled to hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Assembly elections have been slated for February 6, 2026. In the last seven days, there have been cases of political violence in no less than seven states, with the latest in Lagos, where several supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) were injured after suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised on Thursday by the party for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. There was also an incident in Zamfara State during an All Progressives Congress (APC) primary. INEC will obey court verdict on Atiku’s eligibility – Amupitan How 4 UNN students died after graduation party Other states that recorded violence within the period included Edo, Delta, Gombe and Cross River states. The incidents have been more frequent this year, with states like Katsina, Kebbi, Enugu, Ekiti, Ondo, Ebonyi, Osun and Nasarawa states all experiencing various forms of political violence. Prominent political actors have also threatened voters in ways that raised concerns over free, fair and credible polls in 2027. The National Peace Committee revealed recently that reports spanning August 19 to October 27 documented 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. It also observed that political violence and thuggery led the violations with 33 incidents, closely followed by 29 cases of misinformation and disinformation and identified Kaduna, Edo, and Enugu as serious flashpoints for electoral violence. The European Union (EU) also expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of Nigeria’s general elections. EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, noted that these threats undermined democratic progress and discouraged citizens from participating freely in the electoral process.
